content.text: One more check: how the component tests start.

The embedding e2e tests are in four groups. Each group loads Metabase into a host page in a different way. ## Where the tests are ```text e2e/ ├── test/scenarios/embedding/ # 46 specs, normal Cypress e2e │ ├── *.cy.spec.js|ts # 12 specs: static (JWT) embed, interactive (full-app) embed, admin settings │ ├── shared/ # shared data for the static embed specs │ ├── sdk-iframe-embedding/ # 16 specs: embed.js (modular / "simple" embed) at run time │ ├── sdk-iframe-embedding-setup/ # 13 specs: the "Embed" wizard UI that makes the snippet │ ├── embedding-theme-editor/ # 3 specs: theme editor, theme list, upsell │ └── setup-guide/ # 1 spec ├── test-component/scenarios/embedding-sdk/ # 58 specs: React SDK, mounted with Cypress component testing ├── embedding-sdk-host-apps/ # 5 real host apps (Vite, Next 15 x2, Angular 20, data app) └── test-host-app/ # specs that run against those host apps ├── shared/compatibility.cy.spec.ts └── data-apps/ # 4 specs ``` ## How each group loads the embed ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph A["1. Static / interactive embed"] A1[spec] -->|visitEmbeddedPage / visitFullAppEmbeddingUrl| A2["/embed/... URL with signed JWT
or full app in an iframe"] end subgraph B["2. embed.js (sdk-iframe-embedding)"] B1[spec] -->|loadSdkIframeEmbedTestPage| B2[test HTML page] -->|script tag| B3[embed.js] --> B4[iframe to Metabase] end subgraph C["3. React SDK component tests"] C1[spec] -->|mountSdkContent| C2["SDK component in the Cypress
component runner"] -->|API calls| C3[real backend] end subgraph D["4. Host apps"] D1[spec] --> D2[Docker host app
Vite / Next / Angular] --> D3[real SDK package] --> D4[backend] end ``` ## Main helpers ```text support/helpers/ ├── e2e-embedding-helpers.js # group 1: visitEmbeddedPage, getSignedJwtForResource, publishChanges ├── e2e-embedding-iframe-sdk-helpers.ts # group 2: prepareSdkIframeEmbedTest, loadSdkIframeEmbedTestPage, │ # getSimpleEmbedIframeContent ├── e2e-embedding-iframe-sdk-setup-helpers.ts # group 2: the setup wizard └── embedding-sdk-component-testing/ # group 3: mountSdk, mountSdkContent, guest-embed helpers ``` ## How to run each group ```text bun/yarn test-cypress # groups 1 and 2 (normal e2e) CYPRESS_TESTING_TYPE=component yarn test-cypress # group 3 (component config, # specPattern = e2e/test-component/scenarios/**) SDK_TEST_SUITE=vite-6-host-app-e2e \ yarn test-cypress-host-sample-apps # group 4 (starts Docker containers first) ``` The host-app runner also runs the external sample apps (`shoppy-e2e`, `metabase-nextjs-sdk-embedding-sample-e2e`, and others) with the same `SDK_TEST_SUITE` switch. ## Summary | Group | What it tests | Count | |---|---|---| | Static / interactive | Signed `/embed` URLs, parameters, full-app iframe | 12 | | embed.js runtime | Auth, guest tokens, theming, downloads, custom elements | 16 | | embed.js setup wizard | Pick the entity, experience, and options, then get the code | 13 | | Theme editor + setup guide | Admin UI | 4 | | SDK component | React SDK parts: questions, dashboards, Metabot, touch, React versions | 58 | | Host apps | Real framework apps, compatibility, data apps | 5 | result: Embedding e2e tests are in 4 groups (static/interactive iframe, embed.js, React SDK component tests, Docker host apps), about 120 specs in total. Most are in `e2e/test/scenarios/embedding/` and `e2e/test-component/scenarios/embedding-sdk/`.
I only care about e2e/scenarios (standard e2e tests), do they have any special characteristics compared with other e2e tests?
You asked if the standard e2e specs in `e2e/test/scenarios/embedding/` are different from other e2e specs. I will compare their setup, helpers, and tags with the rest of the suite.

content.text:
Yes. The specs in `e2e/test/scenarios/embedding/` use the same runner, the same `restore()` snapshots, and the same `H.*` helpers as other e2e specs. But they have six special characteristics.

## 1. The test visits a page that the test itself makes, not the Metabase app

A normal spec opens a Metabase route. An embedding spec opens an embed URL or a fake host page, and then looks inside an iframe.

```text
normal spec                       embedding spec (embed.js)
  cy.visit("/question/1")           cy.intercept("GET", "/sdk-iframe-test-page", { body: <generated HTML> })
  cy.findByText(...)                cy.visit("/sdk-iframe-test-page")
                                      <script src="embed.js">
                                      window.metabaseConfig = {...}
                                      <metabase-dashboard dashboard-id=1>
                                    getSimpleEmbedIframeContent()   ← waits 40 s for iframe[data-iframe-loaded]
                                      .findByText(...)
```

The Metabase host page is used as the origin, so the specs do not need `cy.origin` or cross-origin settings (0 specs use them).

## 2. Most specs sign out after setup

```text
setup (as admin)                     test (as anonymous visitor)
  restore()                            visitEmbeddedPage(payload)
  cy.signInAsAdmin()                     cy.exec("node e2e-jwt-sign.js ...")   ← signs the JWT in Node
  activateToken("pro-self-hosted")       cy.signOut()                          ← always
  PUT /api/setting/enable-embedding-*    cy.visit("/embed/dashboard/<jwt>#...")
  publish card / dashboard
```

The SDK specs log in with JWT. `mockAuthProviderAndJwtSignIn` intercepts the fake auth provider URL and returns a signed user JWT. Guest embed specs set `embedding-secret-key` to a known secret.

## 3. Setup is mostly in one helper

The 16 specs in `sdk-iframe-embedding/` do not call `restore()` directly. They call `prepareSdkIframeEmbedTest()`, which does all of the setup:

```text
prepareSdkIframeEmbedTest({ withToken, enabledAuthMethods, signOut })
  restore()
  cy.signInAsAdmin()
  activateToken("bleeding-edge")           ← default
  PUT enable-embedding-simple
  intercept card / dashcard / dashboard queries
  setupMockAuthProviders  (jwt | saml | api-key)
  mockEmbedJsToDevServer()                 ← local only, see below
```

## 4. They depend on settings and tokens more than other specs

| Pattern | embedding (46 specs) | all other specs (367) |
|---|---|---|
| sets `enable-embedding-*` | 15 | 3 |
| sets `embedding-secret-key` | 6 | 0 |
| uses JWT | 19 | 5 |
| `window.metabaseConfig` | 13 | 0 |
| `@EE` tag | 6 | 3 |
| `@OSS` tag | 9 | 19 |

Some areas have two copies of a spec, one for each edition. For example, `common-ee` and `common-oss-and-starter` are copies, and `guest-embed-ee` and `guest-embed-oss` are copies. They test the same flow on different plans (`starter`, `pro-self-hosted`, `pro-cloud`, or no token).

## 5. Local runs and CI runs load embed.js differently

```text
mockEmbedJsToDevServer()
  if CI → do nothing (use the built embed.js)
  else  → curl localhost:8080/app/embed.js
          if found → redirect embed.js to the rspack dev server (hot reload)
```

Thus, a local run can test embed.js code that is different from the code in CI.

## 6. The static-embed specs use shared fixture data

```text
embedding/
├── embedding-questions.cy.spec.js  ──imports──▶ shared/embedding-questions.js
├── embedding-dashboard.cy.spec.js  ──imports──▶ shared/embedding-dashboard.js
└── ...                                          (question/dashboard definitions, not tests)
```

## Same as other specs

- They run with the normal `test-cypress` command and use the same CI shards. They are not in a separate CI job.
- They use the same snapshots and `H.*` helpers, and the same `@external` tag (3 specs).
